item: Pool, disk and unlock follow-up: every finding of the reviews of #1287, #1289 and #1293
key_paths: src/api/unlock.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; src/database/pool_watch.py; src/scheduler/storage_guard.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/taskmanager.js; src/static/unlock.js; tests/test_unlock_recovery_progress.py; tests/test_pool_watch_endpoint.py; tests/test_storage_guard_io_error.py
summary: The follow-up the coordinator asked for after three merged PRs. Unlock: the verify checkpoint sets busy_timeout 0 first, so a reader on the file no longer makes it wait 30 s holding the write lock; the recovery floor sits above the journal-size limit in force and the sentence says up to; unlock attempts run one at a time; a failed write-back is a WARNING; recovery_estimate refuses a size that is not a real positive number. Pool and guard: standing holders count the corpus pool only (a read-snapshot export no longer takes a corpus slot off the headroom); an I/O error is classified on the driver's exception and keeps only its first line (SQL and bound parameters stay out of the status payload and the bundle); the drive is read once a second at most per incident, never two readings at once; a failing drain is a WARNING once and quiet while it repeats; the pool's route label is the route template; the pool's recent invalidations ride the write-gate report, their WARNING is throttled and their message is formatted outside the lock. Page: the preview note is silent between refresh cycles and a computation that keeps failing says so (new sentence, 12 locales). Ledger: R118 recorded, LESSONS corrected where the reviews found claims the measurements did not support (the stall of a wrong passphrase is not a per-GiB figure), #1283's summary regains past threading.TIMEOUT_MAX. Each fix has a test that fails under its mutant.
